newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia noon rubber down on bearish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia noon rubber down on bearish sentiment.

text.p: Continued lack of consumer demand, further falls in Tokyo and uncertainty in the Thai baht dragged down prices at noon, dealers said.

"Sentiment continues bearish. Prices are falling and buyers are keeping away from the market," a dealer at a trading firm said. "We are also concerned about the baht and what the Thai government will do. This may affect bank lending to the local rubber industry."
Dealers said little interest was seen from the Far East as buyers were hoping for prices to dip further due to the bearishness in Tokyo market.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 315 cents, SMR L at 295, SMR 10 at 248, SMR 20 at 246 and latex at 215-216.
July RSS One buyer eased 1.50 cents to 268.50 cents ($1.06) a kg and July SMR 20 buyer was down 2.50 cents at 247.
"Supply is not really improving much as some tappers are believed to have stopped tapping because of low market prices," another dealer said.

A Malaysia-based shipping agent quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $800 per TEU (or 20-ft container), and $1,700 per two-TEU containers (or 40-ft container). --Tan Lee Lee -603 275-6834 ($1-2.5200 ringgit)
